experiments.hypothesis: Indian-market visitors landing on motoquant.in don't try the simulator because the hero CTA copy doesn't tell them what they'll get. Variant B replaces 'Try the simulator' with a verb-result CTA naming the outcome ('See your bike's quarter-mile ET') — should lift simulator-runs / landing-visitor.
experiments.implementation_notes: Client-side useSearchParams() in web/app/page.js. Same canonical URL, same href (/simulator), same h1, same meta — SEO-safe. data-exp/data-variant attributes on the Link for analytics attribution.
experiments.decision_criteria: Ship variant B as new control if simulator-runs/visitor lifts ≥15% with p<0.05 over ≥200 samples per arm. Roll back if bounce rate increases >10% or CTR decreases. No decision before 200 samples per arm.

experiments.hypothesis: Pricing-page Pro CTA 'Subscribe to Pro' is high-commitment language that triggers loss-aversion on the click. Variant B 'Start Pro · 7-day refund' reframes the action as a low-risk trial start with the risk-reversal embedded on the button itself, so the eye doesn't have to drift to the smaller caption below. Should lift Pro checkout-init / pricing-visitor.
experiments.implementation_notes: Client-side useSearchParams() in web/app/pricing/page.js. Same canonical URL, same checkout endpoint, same h1, same meta — SEO-safe. data-exp/data-variant attributes on the Pro button for analytics attribution. Studio CTA unchanged (single-variable rule). EXP-001 is on landing-hero so no page conflict.
experiments.decision_criteria: Ship variant B as new control if pro_checkout_init/visitor lifts ≥15% with p<0.05 over ≥200 samples per arm AND razorpay_checkout_completion does not drop >5% (we want trial intent, not abandoned-cart inflation). Roll back if Studio cannibalisation increases >10% (refund-anchor stealing higher-tier intent). No decision before 200 samples per arm.

experiments.hypothesis: Indian-market visitors who land on /simulator see Hayabusa pre-selected, which feels aspirational but disconnected — the 'is this for my bike?' cognitive cost is non-trivial when a 220 hp 1340cc liter bike is pre-loaded for a visitor whose actual bike is a 200cc commuter. Variant B defaults to Pulsar NS 200 (the highest-volume Indian commuter most likely to match a /simulator visitor's actual ride). If the localised default reduces friction, simulator-runs / visitor-to-simulator should rise without compromising the SEO-stable Hayabusa control on the canonical URL.
experiments.variant_a: Hayabusa pre-selected (existing control, matches OG copy + SEO keywords)
experiments.implementation_notes: Client-side useSearchParams() in web/app/simulator/page.js, wrapped in <Suspense> per the static-prerender rule. Variant-aware selection done in pickDefaultBikeForVariant() — name-substring match against the DB bike list so catalog reshuffles (Hayabusa Gen1 vs 2008-2012 vs 2021-2024 model rows) don't break the variant. Falls back to bikes[0] (existing pre-EXP-003 alphabetical-first behaviour) if no name match. data-exp/data-variant attributes on the bike-picker Card for analytics attribution. Same canonical URL, same h1, same meta — SEO-safe. EXP-001 is on landing-hero, EXP-002 is on /pricing — no page conflict.
experiments.decision_criteria: Ship variant B as new control if simulator-runs/visitor lifts ≥15% with p<0.05 over ≥200 samples per arm AND bike_picker_change_rate does not increase by >20% (we want a useful default, not just a default the user immediately overrides). Roll back if simulator_page_bounce_rate increases >10% (Pulsar default may push aspirational-segment visitors away). No decision before 200 samples per arm. Note the SEO consideration: variant A stays canonical because layout.js metadata + OG copy reference Hayabusa; if B wins we still keep Hayabusa as the explicit ?variant=A path so search-result CTR isn't disrupted by the default flip.

experiments.hypothesis: Blog readers who reach the 2nd H2 of a long-form physics post are at a natural mid-scroll section break and have already invested ~3 minutes of reading attention. The current end-of-post CTA fires only after they finish — by which point they are mentally exiting. Placing a pull-quote-style simulator CTA after the 2nd H2 (with copy + href identical to the end-of-post card so placement is the only variable) should lift simulator-runs / blog-post-visitor without cannibalising the end-of-post CTA, because mid-scroll click-throughs come from a reader cohort that would otherwise have bounced before the article end.
experiments.variant_a: End-of-post CTA only (existing pattern — single card after final paragraph)
experiments.variant_b: End-of-post CTA + pull-quote-style inline CTA after 2nd H2 (mid-scroll)
experiments.implementation_notes: Client-side useSearchParams() in web/app/blog/the-physics-of-a-perfect-launch/InlineSimCta.js, wrapped in <Suspense> per the static-prerender rule (page.js stays a server component so metadata + OG tags still flow through SSG). Variant A renders a hidden span placeholder so the DOM tree is identical except for the inline CTA block itself — no layout shift on control. Variant B injects the CTA after the 2nd H2 (block-counter in the Prose function). Same canonical URL, same h1, same meta — SEO-safe. Inline CTA copy + href deliberately match the end-of-post card so the only variable is placement. data-exp/data-variant attributes on both the wrapper div and the Link element for analytics attribution. End-of-post CTA unchanged on both arms (additive test). EXP-001 is on landing-hero, EXP-002 on /pricing, EXP-003 on /simulator — no page conflict.
experiments.decision_criteria: Ship variant B as new control if simulator-runs/blog-post-visitor lifts ≥15% with p<0.05 over ≥200 samples per arm AND end-of-post CTA absolute CTR does not drop >25% (we want net new clicks, not redistributed clicks — if mid-scroll cannibalises end-of-post entirely we have not actually lifted the page). Roll back if scroll_depth_pct drops >10% (inline CTA causing premature exits) or post_dwell_time_s drops >15% (CTA disrupting reading flow). No decision before 200 samples per arm. If B wins, replicate the pattern across the other 7 blog posts in a follow-up rollout (one post at a time so each replication is its own micro-validation, not a blanket assumption).

experiments.element: Pro tier tag-line (the descriptor under the price)
experiments.hypothesis: Visitors who reach /pricing after running a free simulation already know they want more capability — what they are evaluating is 'will Pro tell me something I can act on?' The current Pro tag line 'Everything you need to go faster' is aspirational but non-specific; it could describe any racing product. Variant B replaces it with a line that names the three specific analytical outputs unique to Pro (unlimited sims, ROI per part, build optimizer) and frames them as a decision tool ('know what each mod does before you buy it'). If specificity reduces the 'is this worth ₹499?' hesitation, pro_checkout_init / pricing_visitor should rise.
experiments.variant_a: Everything you need to go faster.
experiments.variant_b: Unlimited sims, ROI per part, build optimizer — know what each mod does before you buy it.
experiments.implementation_notes:
Client-side useSearchParams() in web/app/pricing/page.js, inside the existing PricingPageInner component which is already wrapped in per the static-prerender rule. Uses a dedicated query param ?exp5=B (not ?variant=B which is owned by EXP-002) so both experiments can be toggled independently without arm contamination — a visitor at ?variant=B&exp5=B gets Pro button variant B + tag line variant B; at ?variant=B alone they get Pro button variant B + tag line control; etc. data-exp='EXP-005' + data-variant={exp5Variant} on the

element for analytics attribution. Control is byte-identical at the default URL (/pricing with no query params). Same canonical URL, same h1, same meta — SEO-safe. EXP-002 covers the Pro button; EXP-005 covers the tag line; no copy overlap.
experiments.decision_criteria: Ship variant B as new control if pro_checkout_init/visitor lifts ≥15% with p<0.05 over ≥200 samples per arm AND razorpay_checkout_completion does not drop >5% (specificity should convert intent, not just inflate clicks). Roll back if studio_cta_cannibalisation_rate increases >10% (specificity may push mid-tier visitors toward Studio, which is a good outcome — but only if Studio conversion also rises, otherwise the effect is cannibalisation not uplift). If both EXP-002 and EXP-005 are running concurrently, use separate ?variant and ?exp5 params for attribution; analyse arms independently before declaring interaction effects. No decision before 200 samples per arm.
